full_judgment: 4. Defendant No. 2 (respondent No. 1 herein) contested the said suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. His case, in short, is that after purchase of the case property by a registered kabala dated 20.06.1955 he constructed semi pucca room made of bricks and corrugated iron and remained in possession thereof from 1976-87 by letting out the same as mess and in 1987 he let out the same to Safiuzzaman at a monthly rental of Tk. 1,100/-. The rent was paid upto 1996. As Saifuzzaman stopped payment of rent since May, 1996, defendant No. 2 filed Small Causes Court Suit (S.C.C. Suit) No. 4 of 1997 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka against him for eviction. On the other hand, Saifuzzaman as the plaintiff filed Other Class Suit No. 6 of 1997 against the defendant for specific performance of contract. The two suits were heard simultaneously by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka. The S.C.C. Suit was decreed, but Other Class Suit No. 6 of 1997 was dismissed. Against the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court, in Other Class Suit, the said Saifuzzaman filed First Appeal No. 409 of 1999 and Civil Revision No. 3696 of 1999 against the judgment and decree passed in the S.C.C. Suit before the High Court Division. The Rule issued in Civil Revision No. 3639 of 1999 was discharged on 25.07.2001. Against the judgment and order passed in the said civil revision, Saifuzzaman preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 60 of 2002 before this Division, which was dismissed on 05.05.2003. While taking steps for recovery of khas possession, defendant No. 2 found a sale notice dated 15.08.2003 published in The Daily Ittefaq in respect of the suit property. After that, defendant No. 2 through his Advocate inquired into the matter, who after going through the record in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka came to know that one Feroza Begum of 97/1, Sukrabad, Mohammadpur, Proprietor of Padma Bastra Bitan applied to the plaintiff-Bank for sanctioning a loan of Tk. 1,00,000/(one lac). The plaintiff-Bank sanctioned the loan and as a security of the said loan the suit property was shown to have been mortgaged by defendant No. 2 on 08.06.1987. As Feroza Begum failed to repay the loan the plaintiff-Bank filed the case against the attorney of Feroza Begum and the other defendants. Defendant No. 2 never lived at 184/2/A, Tejkunipara and he never knew any one named Feroza Begum. Defendant No. 2 did neither execute nor register any deed of mortgage in respect of the suit property in favour of the plaintiff Bank and he never deposited any deed with the plaintiff-Bank. Defendant No. 2 never went to the plaintiff-Bank which also did not issue any notice to him to repay the loan as mentioned in the plaint. Saifuzzaman, the tenant of the defendant No. 2, has been living in the suit property. The son of the bharatia Saifuzzaman participated in the alleged auction of the case property. Saifuzzaman in connivance with the staff of the plaintiff-Bank created the forged mortgage deed. Defendant No. 3 and the auction purchases Khairul Anam Faruki and Jinat Ashrafi are the men of Saifuzzaman and they are also necessary parties to be impleaded in the suit. Neither defendant No. 2 stood as a guarantor to the plaintiff bank for the loan availed of by defendant No. 1 nor he executed the mortgaged deed. As such the plaintiff-Bank was not entitled to get any relief against him and the suit was liable to be dismissed against him.
